title: Halifax-Style Donairs
subtitle: Nova Scotia's late-night classic: thin slices of seasoned beef in warm pitas with tomato, onion and the famous sweet garlic sauce
imageAlt: Two donairs wrapped in foil-lined pitas with sliced beef, tomato, onion and white sweet sauce on a cream plate with a navy napkin
servingsNote: 6 donairs: dinner for one big eater + one hungry eater, plus 2 lunches

beforeYouStart.text: Knead the meat hard for 5 minutes until it turns sticky and paste-like. That's what makes thin, tight donair slices.
Make the sauce first so it can chill and thicken.

items.name: pitas
items.note: pocketless Greek-style if you can find them

steps.title: Sweet sauce
steps.text: Whisk the evaporated milk, sugar and garlic powder until the sugar dissolves. Slowly drizzle in the vinegar while whisking; it thickens as you go. Chill.

steps.title: Knead
steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C (350°F). Mix the flour, paprika, onion powder, garlic powder, dried oregano, salt and pepper. Knead it into the beef with your hands for 5 minutes, slapping it into the bowl, until sticky and smooth.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Shape into a tight, smooth loaf about 20 cm long and set it on a rack over a foil-lined baking sheet. Bake 60–70 minutes, turning once, until 71°C (160°F) in the centre. Cool 10 minutes, then slice as thinly as you can.

steps.title: Sear
steps.text: Brown the slices in a dry skillet over medium-high, 1 minute a side, until crisp at the edges. Warm the pitas in the same pan.

steps.title: Build
steps.text: Pile the beef on the pitas, add tomato and onion and drizzle with plenty of sweet sauce. Roll up in foil or parchment.

fixIt.fix: Add vinegar slowly, a little at a time, and chill 30 minutes; it sets as it cools.
It wasn't kneaded long enough. Knead until it looks like a smooth paste.
Chill the cooked loaf 30 minutes, then slice with a sharp knife.

saleTip: Evaporated milk is often 2 for $3 at No Frills; ground beef family packs are cheapest per kilo.
swap: Pocket pitas work too; warm them and fold. Ground lamb for half the beef, cooked to 71°C (160°F).
leftovers: Freeze sliced meat flat; it reheats in minutes in a hot pan.
doneness: Ground beef loaf at 71°C (160°F) in the centre (Health Canada, ground beef).
source: Based on tested home Halifax donair methods (Food Network Canada, Nova Scotia home recipes): a kneaded, spiced ground beef loaf baked at 180°C, sliced thin and seared; evaporated milk, sugar and vinegar sweet sauce. Kept mild.
prepAhead: Make the sweet sauce up to 4 days ahead.
Bake the loaf a day ahead; chilled, it slices even thinner.
reheat: Slices in a hot skillet 1–2 minutes a side, until 74°C (165°F).

basic.note: Donair meat with sweet sauce in pitas; no dried oregano or raw onion.

fancy.note: Donair fries on the side: fries topped with donair meat, mozzarella and sweet sauce.

addSteps.title: Donair fries
addSteps.text: Bake the fries as the package says. Top with some sliced donair meat and the mozzarella and broil 2 minutes until melted. Drizzle with sweet sauce.

plating: Wrap each donair halfway in foil, the Halifax way.
Extra sweet sauce in a dish.

why.1-0: Evaporated milk thickens with vinegar into the signature sweet, garlicky sauce.
why.0-1: A spoon of flour helps the kneaded meat bind into a sliceable loaf.
why.0-2: Sweet paprika gives donair colour and warmth without heat.

funFact: Halifax named the donair its official food in 2015; it was adapted from the Greek gyro in the early 1970s.

keeps.note: freeze sliced meat; the sauce doesn't freeze
